scenarios.label: Sales inquiry
scenarios.brief: The caller asks whether a particular new model and trim is in stock, roughly what it costs, and whether they can test drive it. The salesperson answers in general terms, asks one or two qualifying questions, and offers a test drive time.

scenarios.label: Service appointment
scenarios.brief: The caller books routine service (for example an oil change, a tire rotation, a brake inspection, or a check engine light). The advisor asks for the vehicle and mileage, offers a day and time, and mentions a shuttle or a loaner when it fits.

scenarios.label: Recall question
scenarios.brief: The caller received a recall notice in the mail for the vehicle they own and asks whether it applies, whether it costs anything, and how long it takes. The advisor looks it up from the last six characters of the VIN, confirms the repair is free, and books it. Keep the recall itself generic: do not claim that any real make or model has a specific defect, and do not cite a campaign number.

scenarios.label: Trade-in
scenarios.brief: The caller wants to know what their current vehicle is worth as a trade-in toward a new one. The salesperson asks for the year, mileage and condition, explains that a firm number needs an in-person appraisal, and invites them in.

scenarios.label: Parts order
scenarios.brief: The caller asks the parts counter for a part or accessory (for example all-weather floor mats, wiper blades, a cabin air filter, or a spare key fob), its price and whether it is in stock. The specialist checks, quotes a price, and arranges pickup or an order.

scenarios.label: Recording request: copy
scenarios.brief: After the recording notice, the caller asks why the call is recorded, who can hear it, and how to get a copy of their recording. The advisor explains plainly that calls are recorded for quality and records, that the caller can have a copy, and says they will pass the request to the office manager and call back. Then the caller briefly handles a small service question.

scenarios.label: Recording request: deletion
scenarios.brief: The caller is uncomfortable that the call is recorded and asks for the recording of this call to be deleted. The salesperson says they will note the request and pass it to the manager who handles recordings, without promising anything they cannot do, and asks whether the caller still wants help with their question.

scenarios.label: Hang-up
scenarios.brief: The caller starts asking about a vehicle, the salesperson asks them to hold while they find the right person, and the caller hangs up before anyone comes back. The script ends with the caller muttering that they will try somewhere else.

scenarios.label: Hang-up: screened robocall
scenarios.brief: An automated prerecorded sales pitch calls the dealership's sales line. The salesperson answers; the recording plays a generic pitch for business energy savings without naming any company. The call is cut off by the line's screening announcement.

scenarios.label: After hours
scenarios.brief: The call comes in after the dealership has closed and is answered by its after-hours answering service on the dealership's behalf. The attendant gives the hours, takes the caller's name, callback number and reason, and says the right department will call back when it opens.

scenarios.label: Voicemail
scenarios.brief: No one picks up. The first business turn is the advisor's recorded voicemail greeting. The caller then leaves a message with their name, vehicle, reason for calling, and callback number, and hangs up.
